Title: 竹里馆
Author: 王维, Tang

独坐幽篁里，
弹琴复长啸。
深林人不知，
明月来相照。
content:
Sitting alone in the secluded bamboo grove,
I pluck the zither and give a long whistle.
Deep in the forest no one knows I am here;
The bright moon comes to shine on me.

Notes:
“Long whistle” (changxiao): a drawn-out whistling or chanting practiced by scholars as a form of release and communion with nature.

Title: 商山早行
Author: 温庭筠, Tang

晨起动征铎，客行悲故乡。
鸡声茅店月，人迹板桥霜。
槲叶落山路，枳花明驿墙。
因思杜陵梦，凫雁满回塘。
content:
At dawn I rise and set the journey bells ringing;
A traveler on the road, I grieve for my homeland.
Cockcrow, the moon over a thatched inn;
Footprints in the frost on a plank bridge.
Oak leaves fall on the mountain path;
Trifoliate-orange blossoms brighten the post-station wall.
Then I think of my dream of Duling:
Mallards and wild geese fill the winding pond.

Notes
Duling: a place near Chang’an associated with the poet’s memories of home.
Post-station: an official relay station for travelers and couriers.
